The existence of national or sectoral cybersecurity requirements is closely associated with how

ports engage with incident reporting and response mechanisms. Among respondents who indicate

being subject to such requirements, 69 percent indicate that they must notify a national or sectoral

Computer Security Incident Response Teams (CSIRT) in the event of a cybersecurity incident,

while a further 13 percent report that notification is possible on a voluntary basis. Where such

response teams exist, their role typically includes assessing reported incidents, supporting response

efforts, sharing relevant information with other critical infrastructure operators, competent public

authorities, and, where appropriate, CSIRT counterparts in other countries. This broader information

exchange supports coordinated responses to cyber threats, enables intelligence gathering, and

facilitates risk mitigation beyond individual organizations or national boundaries.

Los Angeles Cyber Resilience Center

The Port of Los Angeles launched its Cyber Resilience Center in January 2022 to serve
